items.proposedAnswer: The cerebellum maintains the posture and balance of the body and coordinates voluntary movements such as walking in a straight line or picking up a pencil.

items.q: Compare nervous control and hormonal control in animals.
items.proposedAnswer: Nervous control uses electrical impulses that travel along nerves and give quick, short-lived responses. Hormonal control uses chemicals carried by blood, which act more slowly but have longer-lasting effects.
keyPoints: Hormonal: chemicals in blood, slower, long-lasting

items.q: What is regeneration? Name an organism that shows it.
items.proposedAnswer: Regeneration is the ability of an organism to grow back lost parts or even a whole new individual from a piece. Planaria and Hydra show regeneration.

items.q: How does the male gamete reach the egg in a flower after the pollen lands on the stigma?
items.proposedAnswer: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube through the style down to the ovary. The male gamete passes through the tube to the ovule, where it fuses with the egg cell.

items.q: What is meant by variation?
items.proposedAnswer: Variation means the differences between the individuals of a species, such as in height, colour or other characteristics.

items.q: Why was the garden pea a good choice for Mendel's experiments?
items.proposedAnswer: It has many easily seen contrasting traits, a short life cycle, produces many seeds, and can be self-pollinated or cross-pollinated in a controlled way.

items.q: State two differences between a real image and a virtual image.
items.proposedAnswer: A real image can be obtained on a screen, while a virtual image cannot. A real image is formed when light rays actually meet and is usually inverted, whereas a virtual image is formed by rays that only appear to meet and is erect.
keyPoints: Real image can be caught on a screen

items.q: What is the function of the optic nerve?
items.proposedAnswer: The optic nerve carries the electrical signals produced in the retina to the brain, where they are interpreted as images.

items.q: What is hypermetropia? State one cause.
items.proposedAnswer: Hypermetropia is a defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly but not nearby ones, since the image forms behind the retina. It is caused by a weak eye lens with a long focal length or an eyeball that is too short.
keyPoints: A cause such as a short eyeball
